hero.headline: Brightline station in downtown Stuart unlikely after Martin County denied federal funding
hero.teaser: Martin County will not receive federal funding for a proposed Brightline station in downtown Stuart through the Intercity Passenger Rail Program, making the future of the project u
hero.body:
Martin County will not receive federal funding for a proposed Brightline station in downtown Stuart through the Intercity Passenger Rail Program, making the future of the project uncertain. The railroad bridge project in Stuart, a replacement for the century-old St.

U.S. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., who represents District 21 in the U.S. House of Representatives, said additional federal funding for a station is unlikely. Mast raised concerns about the structure of the proposed project, saying it is extremely problematic that the potential Brightline station would be entirely taxpayer-funded at the various levels, from federal all the way down to the local municipalities, with Brightline not putting anything into it. He said the company had no interest in examining whether they should build something less expensive.

John Dial, a mariner and owner of At the Helm Training, welcomed the bridge funding but expressed reservations about using public money for a private company's station. Christopher Vitale, the manager at the Old Colorado Inn, said a Brightline station would benefit the local economy and expressed hope that community leaders find another path forward. Jenna McGrew, a local resident, said federal tax dollars should go to things that help better the community, and a Brightline station would definitely help better the community.

Martin County released a statement saying it is pleased to see the announcement of federal funding for a Brightline station in Cocoa Beach, as well as additional federal funding awarded to the City of Stuart for the St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge. The county said it recognizes the importance of supporting and investment in transportation projects that benefit residents, strengthen local businesses and contribute to the continued economic vitality of the state. Tony Scozzafava, a resident, said he hopes the county can find an alternative approach to secure funding for the station.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested on sexual activity with minor charges after SWAT operation
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested Virgil Jason Vinz early Thursday after executing a search warrant at a home on SW Jaslo Avenue.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested a 48-year-old man Thursday morning on multiple charges involving a minor after the department's SWAT team served a search warrant at a home in the 900 block of Southwest Jaslo Avenue. Officers took Virgil Jason Vinz into custody without incident around 6 a.m. He faces five counts of sexual activity with a minor, a second-degree felony under Florida law, and six counts of contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child, a first-degree misdemeanor.

Neighbors reported hearing loud booms before seeing officers outside the home. Police spokesperson Brandon Martinez said the sounds were not gunshots but Noise Flash Diversionary Devices used during the SWAT team's entry. He said the devices are used for the safety of both officers and individuals during high-risk operations. Martinez said officers take any case involving a child very seriously but are limited in what they can discuss while the case remains active.

Martinez said officers are familiar with Vinz from previous encounters but emphasized the current case is separate from any prior incidents. Court records show Vinz pleaded no contest and was adjudicated guilty in 2023 on charges of battery on a law enforcement officer and contributing to the delinquency of a child. Records also show he later violated probation before completing Mental Health Court in October 2024.

Vinz remained in the St. Lucie County Jail as of Thursday night, with bond pending. Authorities have not said what evidence was recovered from the home or what prompted the investigation.

cards.body:
Republican nominee Byron Donalds promised to reduce Florida property insurance costs by another 20% to 25% through regulatory changes and defended data center development as the governor's race shifts from the August primary to a November contest against Democratic nominee David Jolly. In a recent interview, Donalds outlined positions on property taxes, insurance, school vaccine requirements and data centers that now define the campaign.

Donalds supports Amendment 3, which would increase the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 for Floridians who establish permanent residency by the end of 2026. The measure would also lower the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%. New residents would face a five-year phase-in before qualifying for the full exemption. A legislative financial analysis estimates the amendment would reduce local non-school property-tax revenue by nearly $5 billion in its first full fiscal year, with the recurring impact projected to approach $11.9 billion by the 2031-32 fiscal year. Donalds called the amendment a first step and suggested Florida should eventually consider a multi-tiered taxing system that treats counties differently based on property values and economic output. He did not spell out how the tiers would work or how local governments would replace lost revenue.

On insurance, Donalds said regulatory changes could push costs down another 20% to 25%. His ideas include changing the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund, lowering reinsurance costs and making home-hardening grants more efficient. Donalds specifically pointed to the catastrophe fund's 25% cash buildup factor, which insurers pay on top of actuarially calculated premiums. He said the state could eliminate the charge or create a formula that turns it down when the fund has healthy reserves and raises it when the balance falls. Donalds did not provide an independent analysis showing how the changes would produce the promised savings or how quickly homeowners would see them.

Data center development has become the main division with Jolly. Donalds supports building the facilities with safeguards including closed-loop water-cooling systems, protections for residential utility customers and restrictions keeping large centers away from homes. Jolly has proposed a statewide moratorium while Florida studies environmental protections, long-term economic effects and privacy and security concerns connected to AI. A Seeking Rents analysis of state campaign-finance records estimated that roughly $5.8 million in donations and outside spending connected to AI investors, utilities and data-center interests had benefited Donalds. A Gallup survey released in May found 71% of Americans opposed building an AI data center in their local area, including 48% who strongly opposed it.

cards.body:
A motorist driving an SUV sustained traumatic injuries after colliding with a northbound Brightline train late Thursday morning in Hobe Sound. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Fire Rescue, the crash happened near the intersection of Southeast Dixie Highway and Southeast Crossrip Street at around 11 a.m. The man driving the SUV was transported to the hospital.

Photos from the scene show multiple firefighters aiding the victim beside the SUV with heavy front-end damage while bystanders watched. Deputies advised motorists to avoid the area while investigators were at the scene. The train tracks were temporarily shut down but have since reopened. All lanes of traffic have reopened.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.body:
Martin County will not receive federal funding for a proposed Brightline station in downtown Stuart through the Intercity Passenger Rail Program, making the future of the project uncertain. The railroad bridge project in Stuart, a replacement for the century-old St.

U.S. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., who represents District 21 in the U.S. House of Representatives, said additional federal funding for a station is unlikely. Mast raised concerns about the structure of the proposed project, saying it is extremely problematic that the potential Brightline station would be entirely taxpayer-funded at the various levels, from federal all the way down to the local municipalities, with Brightline not putting anything into it. He said the company had no interest in examining whether they should build something less expensive.

John Dial, a mariner and owner of At the Helm Training, welcomed the bridge funding but expressed reservations about using public money for a private company's station. Christopher Vitale, the manager at the Old Colorado Inn, said a Brightline station would benefit the local economy and expressed hope that community leaders find another path forward. Jenna McGrew, a local resident, said federal tax dollars should go to things that help better the community, and a Brightline station would definitely help better the community.

Martin County released a statement saying it is pleased to see the announcement of federal funding for a Brightline station in Cocoa Beach, as well as additional federal funding awarded to the City of Stuart for the St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge. The county said it recognizes the importance of supporting and investment in transportation projects that benefit residents, strengthen local businesses and contribute to the continued economic vitality of the state. Tony Scozzafava, a resident, said he hopes the county can find an alternative approach to secure funding for the station.

cards.headline: SUV driver hospitalized with traumatic injuries after collision with Brightline train in Hobe Sound
cards.teaser: A motorist driving an SUV sustained traumatic injuries after colliding with a northbound Brightline train late Thursday morning near Southeast Dixie Highway and Southeast Crossrip Street in Hobe Sound.
cards.body:
A motorist driving an SUV sustained traumatic injuries after colliding with a northbound Brightline train late Thursday morning in Hobe Sound. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Fire Rescue, the crash happened near the intersection of Southeast Dixie Highway and Southeast Crossrip Street at around 11 a.m. The man driving the SUV was transported to the hospital.

Photos from the scene show multiple firefighters aiding the victim beside the SUV with heavy front-end damage while bystanders watched. Deputies advised motorists to avoid the area while investigators were at the scene. The train tracks were temporarily shut down but have since reopened. All lanes of traffic have reopened.
